decision.statement: Use an opaque theorem-level IncarnationId for one allocation lifetime, enforce trace/run-local no-reuse through an explicit ever-issued ledger and witnessed allocation boundary, retain current-registry freshness as the paper-compatible local premise, and define alpha-renaming as an explicit permutation action over every name-bearing field. Runtime atom reuse is admitted only through an explicit generation/allocation-event refinement.
decision.paper_fidelity_status: logical-repair/refinement-profile; literal O-Remove-to-O-Insert atom reissue remains a lower-level profile
decision.root_representation: ParentRef = Option IncarnationId; none is a synthetic root fixed by alpha
decision.ledger_boundary: orchestration/trace metadata paired with RawState when allocation semantics is evaluated; excluded from default ADR-03 coeffect observation unless an explicit name-aware observation is selected
decision.freshness_observation_rule: freshness-sensitive allocation applicability and same-rule preservation use the (RawState, ledger/TraceMeta) product or an externally labelled orchestration relation; default CoreStateObs must not erase the ledger for those claims
decision.relation_split: lifecycle relation on RawState excludes freshness-sensitive allocation steps; orchestration relation on (RawState, TraceMeta) carries allocation/retirement labels, and any unified Step must include the ledger in its state/observation

freshness_and_allocation.allocation_allowed: CurrentFresh registry n ∧ EverFresh ledger n ∧ ParentAllowed registry parent
freshness_and_allocation.successful_update: registry' = insert n registry and everIssued' = insert n everIssued
freshness_and_allocation.retirement_update: remove/retire changes current registry only; everIssued is monotone
freshness_and_allocation.scope: no-reuse is enforced within one modeled run/trace identity domain; an epoch reset requires a fresh namespace and no cross-boundary references
freshness_and_allocation.allocation_representation: relational or proof-witnessed; no deterministic min/max allocator in the theorem core
freshness_and_allocation.supply: optional FreshSupply chooses Option N and reports exhaustion; total-allocation theorems require an explicit availability premise
freshness_and_allocation.supply_equivariance: an executable supply is outside the alpha theorem core unless it carries a permutation action and equivariance law
freshness_and_allocation.nested_registration: allocation labels/history must expose every D47/iterator-created child and its parent/owner
freshness_and_allocation.stale_handle_policy: a retirement/inverse handle captures the IncarnationId allocation, never a later reissued atom
freshness_and_allocation.transition_carrier: allocation-aware semantics use (RawState, NameLedger/TraceMeta) or an equivalent orchestration product; RawState alone is not Markov for lifetime freshness

parent_boundary.none_meaning: synthetic root marker, not a registry/provider entry
parent_boundary.registration_order: separate birth/allocation-event index; never order by the representation of an opaque ID
parent_boundary.support_cycle_status: not solved here; late-registration/support cycles remain BD-SUPPORT/BD-CONTROL

renamed_fields: trace names, episode keys, precedence/support indices
unchanged_fields: payload/code values only under identity-opacity assumption
alpha_action.payload_policy: name-neutral payloads are the spike specialization; ID-bearing behavior, accumulators, ambient values, handles, or hashes require Rename* actions and interpreter equivariance
alpha_action.observation_relation: separate from ADR-01 CoreStateObs, LifecycleObs, and EraseControl
alpha_action.global_vs_local: global permutation is the L56 form; T73 may first use a finite support bijection and must provide an extension/finite-action lemma when a global permutation is required

runtime_refinement.map: the spike uses globally injective encode : RuntimeIdentity Atom Generation → IncarnationId; an integration may restrict this to an explicitly admissible allocation domain
runtime_refinement.reuse: same atom with a new generation must map to a distinct incarnation
runtime_refinement.entry_id: separate loader/configuration identity; replacing one entry allocates a new incarnation
runtime_refinement.status: interface/smoke theorem compiled; concrete runtime correspondence and target-hash opacity deferred to implementation refinement

trace_and_episode.finite_support: TraceHasFiniteNames is an explicit finite Finset support witness for a declared trace-name support envelope
trace_and_episode.field_coverage: NameTrace requires the initial issued set, listed allocations, actor/parent/reference labels, boundary snapshots, and support linkage to lie in the envelope
trace_and_episode.exact_occurrence_set: the control/trace layer must define the exact union of names occurring in all snapshots/events and either prove equality with the envelope or state the envelope explicitly
trace_and_episode.label_scope: the spike StepLabel is a name-footprint shell; authoritative rule tags and per-allocation owner/parent events are BD-CONTROL obligations
trace_and_episode.no_reuse: allocation list is Pairwise distinct and fresh relative to the initial issued ledger; operational ledger evolution and event coverage are control-layer obligations
trace_and_episode.allocation_completeness: trace allocation list is required to equal the concatenation of label allocation events
trace_and_episode.episode_key: IncarnationId under no-reuse; allocation-event/generation ID otherwise
trace_and_episode.T66: finite trace support and per-ID work/iterator bounds remain explicit theorem hypotheses
trace_and_episode.T73: same ordered orchestration inputs plus a trace/tree alpha witness; not merely equal final configurations
trace_and_episode.name_wf_scope: NameWF in the spike is only the name-boundary fragment (LedgerSound and ParentForest), not full D58 CoreWellFormed
trace_and_episode.rootedness: a parent-rooted/tree theorem requires the selected finite closed-forest/root witness at integration
trace_and_episode.reuse_refinement: reusable runtime atoms still require a separate trace-lifting/refinement theorem before literal-paper reissue semantics is covered
